correctness.rationale: For one vacancy the lane coordinate is an autonomous symmetric continuous-time cycle walk, and longitudinal successes form a conditionally Poisson count. Its long-time variance is the Poisson term plus twice the finite Markov-chain integrated rate covariance. The cycle Poisson equation is solved explicitly by centered prefix sums, with normalization fixed by zero total gradient. Balanced two-valued rates give an integer-height bridge. Parity forces the sharp variance minimum 1/4; the upper bound is equivalent to minimizing a strictly concave sum of pairwise cycle-resistance terms over the integer cyclic-gap simplex. Strict concavity places every minimizer at a contiguous-block vertex. Exactly 18 rational complete-state generator and Poisson-equation checks and 4704 exhaustive finite pattern comparisons passed. These are consistency checks, not the infinite proof. The claim requires strictly positive rates and fixed finite cylinder before long-time limit.

originality.rationale: The identified source model and its uniform/factorized stationarity and current are published. General Markov-modulated Poisson count-variance machinery and cycle Green functions are prior methods. The inspected full texts do not state the exact arbitrary-profile finite-cylinder prefix formula together with the sharp global binary lane-ordering extrema and equality rigidity. The gap is motivated by stationary-order invariance versus temporal noise dependence, rather than a restatement of generic overdispersion. Equivalent older spectral rearrangement and queueing coverage is a residual risk requiring independent bibliographic check.
residual_risks: Older queueing and Markov-modulated Poisson literature might contain the same sharp binary permutation extremum even if not indexed under exclusion terminology.
A general discrete rearrangement theorem for the cycle Green energy might imply the upper bound and equality without this stochastic application.

value.rationale: The observable is a physical integrated transport-activity count, and the exact all-arrangement envelope distinguishes temporal fluctuations from invariant equal-time probabilities and average throughput. The combinatorial optimization is genuinely all-size: alternating and clustered configurations are the unique extrema among exponentially many speed placements, with a sharp excess-noise ratio (m²+2)/3. It gives a finite high-density benchmark for lane-placement effects, with the source model, invariant mean and assumptions explicit. The distinction has relevance to inference from stationary densities and design of dynamically heterogeneous channels. No thermodynamic claim is made.
